tasks.title: the history guard reads a comment, a here-string, a case body and an emitted hook the way the shell does
tasks.description: Close four residuals of the history guard and the shared line-continuation join. (1) join_continuations decides whether `#` starts a comment from the raw previous character; carry a word-start flag instead (an unescaped blank, newline or operator sets it; any other character or an escaped pair clears it; a removed backslash-newline leaves it) and treat `#` as a comment only while it is set. (2) A here-string's reader is recognised only as the first word of its command; find it past the same wrapper list the heredoc reader uses. (3) A `case` pattern's `)` inside a double-quoted substitution closes it early; a body holding a `case` with no `esac` before the close is unreadable (the command goes to the raw-text reading). (4) An emitter whose output is written to a redirect target that carries a quote or expansion, lies under a git hooks directory (.git/hooks/, .husky/, core.hooksPath), or is run later in the same command (sh/bash/source/./path/make) stays graded as the git it spells. Each with a deny case red first and an allow case beside it; SECURITY.md's residual list and CHANGELOG updated.

tasks.title: Review findings: the guards lex operators outside quotes, read only an emitter's phrase, and read a case body instead of giving up
tasks.description:
Phase review findings, all to be fixed. Decisions: (R1) the stage model lexes its own operators, recognising `|`, `>` and the rest only OUTSIDE quotes, so a quoted `>` in a commit message is text. (R2) the phrase pass applies only to a stage whose program is a text emitter (echo, printf), the one program whose arguments are what it prints. (R3) `_substitution_end` tracks `case`/`esac` in command position and treats a `)` inside an open case as a pattern's, so the body is READ rather than handed to the raw-text reading; `_open_case` goes. (R4) the stage model covers a clobber redirect, a group `( )`/`{ }` whose output is piped or redirected, every shell program _config knows plus eval, source of stdin, a program named by a variable, and tee's file operands; a process substitution, a glob or an expansion in a target is unresolvable; hook paths are matched case-insensitively and `.husky/` anywhere. (R5) SECURITY.md names what stays open (a file written by another program such as dd or cp, a phrase assembled at run time) and says here-strings to interpreters are graded. (R6) a here-string to an interpreter that already runs a program (a script file, -c/-e) is data, as the heredoc arm treats it. (R7) a here-string operator glued to the interpreter's name is read. (R8) a unit case pins that a non-keyword `case` leaves a substitution readable. (R9) the CHANGELOG count is removed.

tasks.title: Round-2 review findings: the stage model reads compound commands, comments, receiving groups and nested cases, and over-refuses nothing main allows
tasks.description:
Round-2 review findings, all to be fixed. Decisions: (S1) reserved words are stepped over when finding a stage's program, and if/while/until/for/case ... fi/done/esac form a group whose pipe or redirect reaches every stage inside. (S2) the stage lexer skips a comment (an unquoted `#` at a word start) to the end of its line. (S3) a pipe into a group asks every stage of the receiving group whether it runs its stdin. (S4) case tracking is per nesting level (a stack of the depths where a case opened), so a nested case or one after a parenthesised pattern reads to its real close. (S5) whether an interpreter already runs a program is decided per interpreter: its own inline-program flags (python -c; node -e/-p/--eval/--print; ruby -e; perl -e/-E; php -r) or a script operand with a script extension after its options. (S6) the variable-as-program rule reads only the program word, not a wrapper's operands; a hook-named file counts only in a directory whose name holds 'hook' or under .git/hooks or .husky; a process substitution target runs only when its own command runs its input; ruby/perl script runs and node with options before the script are script runs. (S7) what an emitter prints is its words joined as one line (so a phrase split across arguments is read whole), a cat fed a here-string prints that string, `builtin` is a wrapper, and an inner emitter's substitution contributes what it prints; SECURITY.md's not-followed list is restated from the code.
R1 (med) plugins/audit/hooks/guard-history-rewrite.py:553-559 (_prints_phrases), 493-550 (_stages): _prints_phrases treats a stage as an emitter only when echo or printf is its program word. _stages leaves a reserved word at the head of the stage's words. For `if true; then echo hello > out.txt; fi` the stage is ['then','echo','hello'] with target out.txt, and _prints_phrases returns [] (checked on benign text through _stages/_op_tokens). So consider this shape: an emitter inside a then/else/do body whose own redirect names a hook, or whose output is piped into a shell. The phrase is not read. P83.1 read words[1:] and so did read it; P83.3 dropped it. A second, related case: a compound command (for/while/until/if/case) whose output is piped or redirected after its closing `done`/`fi`/`esac` is not treated as a group. Only the closing-word stage receives `to` or the targets, and the body stages do not. SECURITY.md names neither shape. Not run as an evasion, per the constraint. -> Before program_candidates in _prints_phrases, _runs_input and _tee_targets, strip the leading reserved words (then, do, else, elif, !, the words in _OPENS_COMMAND). In _stages, open a group at if/for/while/until/case and close it at fi/done/esac, the way `{`/`}` are handled, so that a pipe or redirect after the close applies to every member. Add deny cases (an emitter in a then-branch redirected into .git/hooks/, and a loop body piped into a shell) and allow twins (the same written into notes.md).
R2 (med) plugins/audit/hooks/guard-history-rewrite.py:417-491 (_op_tokens): _op_tokens does not know comments. So a group whose inner line ends in a comment holding a close paren (or brace), followed by the real close and a pipe into a shell, leaves the phrase unread. P83.1's change to join_continuations exists exactly to read a comment the way the shell does. This second lexer does not use that rule. -> In _op_tokens, when `#` is unquoted and starts a word (`has` is False, the at_start rule of join_continuations), skip to the end of the line. Add an allow case (an emitter with a comment holding `> $X`) and a deny case (a group whose comment holds `)`, then piped into a shell).
R3 (med) plugins/audit/hooks/guard-history-rewrite.py:613-631 (_output_runs), 562-573 (_runs_input): On the receiving side of a pipe, only the FIRST stage of a group is asked whether it runs its stdin. In `echo hello | (cd x && cat)` the receiver is stage ['cd','x']; the `cat` stage after `&&` is never looked at (checked on benign text). A shell inside a receiving group or brace group, placed after any other command in it, reads the pipe, and the phrase is not read. R4's resolution asked for the receiving side too. gp48/gp49/gp60 cover only the sending side. -> When `to` points at a stage that opens a group, test _runs_input (and _tee_targets) over every member of that group, not just the first. Record group spans in _stages so that _output_runs can find them. Add a deny case: a receiving group whose shell follows a `cd`.
R4 (med) plugins/audit/hooks/guard-history-rewrite.py:633-690 (_substitution_end): The case tracking is one counter, checked only at depth 1. A `case` inside a nested `$(` or `( )` has its pattern `)` read as a close. After a parenthesised pattern `(x)`, the arm's first word is not in command position. Measured on benign bodies (index returned vs the real close): `echo $(case x in a) echo y;; esac) end) tail` gives 33 vs 38; `( case x in a) echo y;; esac ) ) tail` gives 29 vs 31; a nested case after an `(a)` pattern gives 42 vs 57. The first two miss on main as well, so they are not a regression against main. The third was unreadable (raw-text) under P83.1 and is now cut short. The docstring, the CHANGELOG ('a case in command position carries the read past its patterns to its esac') and commit claim 6 all say more than the code does. In a double-quoted substitution, a close taken too early turns the rest of the real body into quoted text that nothing reads. -> Keep a stack of the depths at which a case is open. A `)` ends a pattern exactly when the innermost open case sits at the current depth. Set cmd_pos after any pattern close, parenthesised or not. Add se cases for a case in a nested substitution, a case in a subshell, and a nested case after an `(x)` pattern.
